reason: The no-account, on-device setup is the first thing that's made me even consider another tracker, so I'd read the privacy policy and maybe install the free version. But my first appointment summary is free and logging stays free, so there's nothing I'd need to pay for this month.
objection: Every app says 'private' until it gets bought or changes its policy, and every prediction I've had for my cycles has been useless. Even 'honest ranges' could just mean ranges too wide to help me.
would_change_my_mind: If the free summary actually got my doctor to take me seriously at my next appointment, I'd pay the $7.99 for the one after that.
